title: Virtual Schemas
tagline: Query an external database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Exasol) from Exasol, live, without loading it.
role: Part of the kit. A virtual schema makes the tables of another database appear in Exasol as VS_<NAME>: every query reads the source live, nothing is copied. exakit connect does all of the setup - adapter and JDBC driver downloaded and checksum-verified, staged where the database reads them, the database's Java runtime installed (one restart, asked first), the CONNECTION, adapter script and virtual schema created - and calls it ready only after rows came back.
installed_by: Part of the kit - nothing to install. The first exakit connect installs the database's Java runtime (one restart, asked first).
platforms: Wherever the kit runs the Exasol Personal runtime: macOS, Linux (including WSL) and Windows. On macOS the kit cannot reach the database container, so a source given by host name is reached by its address instead.

quickstart.note: Pick the source type, paste a JDBC URL or the endpoint host name a cloud console shows (host, host:port or host:port/database), or type host, port and database, then the user and password (asked hidden).
Names keep the source's spelling, so they go in double quotes. In PowerShell write \" for each inner quote.
Repairs what a restart or an outside change can undo, then proves the source still answers.

commands.summary: Connect an external database as a virtual schema.
examples: exakit connect postgresql --name sales --url jdbc:postgresql://db.example.com:5432/shop --user reader --schema public --password-file ~/pg.pw

environment.name: EXAKIT_VS_SOURCE
environment.effect: The source type for a run without a terminal: postgresql (pg), mysql, sqlserver (mssql), oracle, exasol.

environment.name: EXAKIT_VS_NAME
environment.effect: The source's name; the virtual schema becomes VS_<NAME>.

environment.name: EXAKIT_VS_JDBC_URL
environment.effect: The connection as a JDBC URL (or postgres:// URI). Any password in it is removed and not used.

environment.name: EXAKIT_VS_HOST, EXAKIT_VS_PORT, EXAKIT_VS_DATABASE
environment.effect: The connection as fields instead of a URL.

environment.name: EXAKIT_VS_USER, EXAKIT_VS_SCHEMA
environment.effect: The source user, and the source schema to expose.

environment.name: EXAKIT_VS_WAREHOUSE, EXAKIT_VS_ROLE (and EXAKIT_VS_<FIELD> for any connector field)
environment.effect: Connector-specific answers, e.g. Snowflake's warehouse and role.

environment.name: EXAKIT_VS_PASSWORD_FILE
environment.effect: A file holding the source password (UTF-8 or UTF-16). There is no --password option.

environment.name: EXAKIT_VS_TLS
environment.effect: verify, encrypt or none. The default is the strongest level the source allows: verify for Exasol (certificate fingerprint), encrypt for the rest. none only for a host on this machine or a private network.

environment.name: EXAKIT_CONFIRM_RUNTIME_UPDATE
environment.effect: 1 (or --yes) consents to the one database restart the Java runtime needs.

environment.name: EXAKIT_VS_DNS_WORKAROUND
environment.effect: 0 stops the kit linking name resolution into the database's Java runtime after each start; sources given by name are then reached by their address.

environment.name: EXAKIT_VS_ALLOW_UNAVAILABLE
environment.effect: 1 lets you try a source marked unavailable (Snowflake) - for checking whether a newer Exasol Personal has fixed what blocks it.

notes: Every virtual schema is readable by the MCP read-only user, so your AI clients can see the source's data the moment it is connected.

The password lives only in the database's CONNECTION object. The kit's admin user can still read it back through a script, as the owner of any Exasol connection can - use a read-only account on the source.

Sources and TLS: PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server are encrypted without verifying the server's certificate (Exasol Personal's import process has no trust store yet); Oracle uses Native Network Encryption; another Exasol is verified by its certificate fingerprint. Snowflake is not available yet: its driver must verify certificates. An unencrypted link is offered only for hosts on this machine or a private network.

Host names: Exasol Personal's Java runtime ships without name resolution. The kit links it in after every database start (the database's boot entry runs exakit start database for that); EXAKIT_VS_DNS_WORKAROUND=0 turns this off and the kit uses IP addresses instead.
localhost inside the database is the database itself. A source on this computer is reached through the container's host address, which exakit connect works out for you.
MySQL's driver (Connector/J) is GPL software the kit downloads onto this machine only.

troubleshooting.remedy: The connection starts inside the database container, not on this PC. Publish the source's port; a company network may be unreachable over a VPN that does not route WSL/Podman traffic.

troubleshooting.symptom: UnknownHostException, or 'could not resolve' after a restart
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit source check <name> re-links name resolution into the Java runtime.

troubleshooting.symptom: The source refused the user name or password
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit source reauth <name> (after a failed first connect: run exakit connect again).

troubleshooting.symptom: object VS_X.ORDERS not found, but the table is listed
troubleshooting.remedy: Names keep the source's spelling: SELECT * FROM VS_X."orders". In PowerShell escape the inner quotes, or use exakit sql --file.
If the source has no TLS: exakit connect <type> --name <name> --tls none (hosts on this machine or a private network only).
